title: Trent opens, 1545
hookLine: a council that answers the reformers and reforms the Church from within

cards: Trent is a small city in a valley of the Alps, on the road between Italy and the German lands. That's why it was chosen: a place the emperor's people and the pope's people could both reach and both accept.
For years, people on more than one side had called for a council. Popes hesitated, rulers quarreled, wars got in the way. At last the bishops gathered in the cathedral there.

teach.b: First, the name. Historians sometimes call this the Counter-Reformation, as if it were only a reaction. Others prefer Catholic Reformation, because reform inside the Church had already started.

Ignatius of Loyola, a wounded soldier, had gathered companions who became the Jesuits. Teresa of Avila would soon reform her Carmelite convents back toward poverty and prayer. Trent gathered that energy into one place.
The bishops decided to work on doctrine and discipline side by side: answer the reformers' questions about faith, and at the same time fix the Church's own house. Not one or the other. Both.
Then, what fixing the house meant.

teach.h: BISHOPS MUST LIVE WITH THEIR PEOPLE.
teach.b: One example: the council insisted that bishops actually live in their dioceses and care for their people, instead of collecting income from far away.
That was one of the abuses from two days ago, addressed by the Church's own council. Last, the root.
Paul writes in Romans, in the Douay-Rheims, "be reformed in the newness of your mind." In the Latin Bible the word is reformamini: be reformed.
For Catholics, reform isn't someone else's word. It's in their own scripture, and it starts with the mind and the heart, not the walls. Over the next days, what Trent actually said.

how: Catholics remember the Council of Trent as the center of the Catholic Reformation; religious orders founded or renewed in that era, like the Jesuits and the Discalced Carmelites, are still active today.

games.q: you're a bishop at Trent's first sessions. some want only doctrine, some only reform. what do you choose?
o: doctrine only; the abuses can wait.
work on both, side by side.
games.why: the council decided to treat doctrine and discipline together: answer the questions and fix the house.

practice: Choose one habit, not your whole life, and picture the moment it usually happens: the time of day, the room, what's in your hand.
Now picture yourself doing the better thing instead, once, in that same moment, small enough that you really could. If you pray, ask for help to begin.

wordCard.voice: Catholic Reformation. The renewal of the Church from inside, gathered at the Council of Trent, answering the reformers and fixing its own house. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: be reformed — Paul's word in Romans 12:2 in the Latin Bible.

carryVoice: Your line: reform from within. Every renewal has a first step, and it can be yours. Day seven hundred eighty-four.
